cover.headline: India's children's-hospital leader, priced below its own history: the bet is that 1,200 new beds fill as well as the last 780
cover.lead: Rainbow runs India's largest paediatric hospital chain (24 hospitals, 2,435 beds excluding the 130 Delhi beds it only staffs), with full-time doctors, a third of its beds in intensive care and a BirthRight maternity brand feeding the children's business. It earns a 32% EBITDA margin after Ind AS 116 (26% after rent) with no bank debt. The catch is occupancy: ~780 beds added in two years pushed it from 55% (FY23) to 41% (Q1FY27), and management now plans ~2,500 more beds (to ~5,000) for ~₹2,200 cr over five years, mostly outside the South. Q1FY27 revenue rose 33% (24% organic). The street values Rainbow on **EV/EBITDA on FY28E (22-28x)**. We forecast EBITDA of ₹625 / 770 / 907 cr and EPS of ₹28.5 / 35.7 / 42.3 for FY27-29E, below the street on margins. Applying **20x to Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹838 cr** (post-Ind AS, lease liabilities in net debt) gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with BUY.** Cross-checks: P/E ₹1,522, DCF ₹1,290. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A specialty that is hard to copy
arguments.p: Children's hospitals need dozens of sub-specialists on call 24/7; Rainbow has 1,075+ full-time doctors, transplant, cardiac and ECMO programmes, and hub-and-spoke density in Hyderabad (~1,000 beds) and Bengaluru (~600). Mature hospitals earned ₹70,662 per occupied bed-day in Q1FY27 (+10%); mothers who deliver at BirthRight stay for paediatric care.

arguments.h: Growth is back, but it is bought with beds
arguments.p: Capacity +26% in a year to 2,435 beds; IP discharges +28%, deliveries +23% in Q1FY27. Occupancy only rose to 41.2% (Q1FY26 40.2%), far below management's 56-58% target. We model revenue +{{F.salesGrowth.0|pct}}, +{{F.salesGrowth.1|pct}}, +{{F.salesGrowth.2|pct}} (FY27-29E), from a bed-by-bed build.

Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin: 26.6% (FY25), 26.3% (FY26), 23.0% (Q1FY27); guidance is 24-25% for FY27. New hospitals lose money for 12-18 months, and Malad, Coimbatore, Gurugram and Pune all open in FY28-29. We model 24.8% / 25.8% / 25.6% pre-Ind AS ({{F.ebitdaMargin.0|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.1|pct}} / {{F.ebitdaMargin.2|pct}} post): FY28E EPS 10% below Prabhudas Lilladher.

arguments.h: Valuation: cheap to history, fair on cash flows
arguments.p: At ₹1,314 the stock trades at 17.7x our FY28E EV/EBITDA, against a 21.5x forward median since listing; hospital peers had de-rated ~7% by 30-Sep-2026, giving 20x and {{dcf.tp|inr}}. Our DCF (₹1,290) is lower: the expansion has to earn its cost of capital for the multiple to hold.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): growth "above 20%" was guided; the first read on the season after a late, deficient monsoon; occupancy and the pre-Ind AS margin (guided 24-25% for FY27).
Ramp-up of the new Bengaluru hospitals (Electronic City breakeven guided within 2-3 months of Jul-2026; HRBR 12-15 months).

Openings: Guntur (50 beds, "in a couple of months" from end-July), Indore (Q3FY27), Malad, Mumbai (Q1FY28), Coimbatore and Gurugram Sector 56 (H2FY28), Gurugram Sector 44 hub (Q1FY29), Pune and Seegehalli (FY29).
The detailed five-year plan management promised, and the terms of the Nellore acquisition and the Malad JV.

sections.title: Hospitals for children and mothers: paediatric super-specialty plus maternity, in hub-and-spoke city networks

blocks.p: Rainbow runs hospitals only for children and women. **Rainbow Children's Hospital** covers everything a sick child may need: emergency and outpatient care, neonatal and paediatric intensive care (NICU/PICU, about a third of beds), and super-specialties up to liver, kidney and bone-marrow transplants, cardiac surgery, neurosurgery, oncology and ECMO. **BirthRight by Rainbow** covers obstetrics, high-risk pregnancy, fetal medicine, fertility (IVF) and gynaecology, inside the same hospitals; obstetrics is ~32% of revenue and IVF ~3.7% (FY26). The two feed each other: a family that delivers at BirthRight comes back when the child falls ill at night. In each city Rainbow builds a **hub** (150-250 beds, complex care) and **spokes** (50-100 beds, emergencies, deliveries, outpatients and level-3 NICU) that refer complex cases to the hub.

Doctors work **full time, on retainer, in teams with 24/7 cover** (1,075+ doctors incl. trainees), unlike most Indian hospitals, which rely on visiting consultants paid per case. Rainbow runs India's largest private paediatric training programme (DNB), which supplies future doctors. In FY26 hospital services were ₹1,449 cr of revenue, pharmacy ₹204 cr and the fee for running the 130-bed Madhukar hospital in Delhi ₹25 cr; ~48% of inpatient revenue was paid in cash and ~52% by insurers.

sections.title: Fewer babies, sicker babies treated privately, and a bed-building boom

blocks.p: India's total fertility rate fell to 1.9 in 2023 (2.0 in 2021-22; replacement 2.1) and the crude birth rate to 18.4 per 1,000 (19.1 in 2022); Bihar 2.8, Delhi 1.2 (Sample Registration System 2023, reported Sep-2025). The number of births is flat to falling, so paediatric and maternity growth comes from more births in organised hospitals, higher acuity and price, not from more babies. That is the central fact of Rainbow's market: it cannot rely on a rising number of children. What is growing is the share of births and childhood illness treated in organised private hospitals with neonatal and paediatric intensive care, insurance cover (52% of Rainbow's inpatient revenue) and the price of complex care. Paediatrics is also seasonal (monsoon and winter infections) and mostly medical rather than surgical, so revenue per patient is lower and less predictable than in adult cardiac or orthopaedic surgery.

sections.title: Revenue = beds × occupancy × ARPOB: beds are up, ARPOB is up, occupancy is down

blocks.p: Hospital revenue is the product of three numbers: **operational beds**, **occupancy** (the share of beds filled each night) and **ARPOB** (average revenue per occupied bed-day; Rainbow includes outpatient and pharmacy revenue, so it is total revenue ÷ occupied bed-days). From FY23 to FY26 weighted operational beds rose 41% (1,186 → 1,677) and ARPOB 23% (₹48,932 → ₹60,141), but occupancy fell from 55.4% to 46.3%, so revenue grew 45% rather than ~70%. ARPOB has risen because the case mix moved to sicker children and more complex procedures, fertility grew, and average stays shortened (2.76 → 2.71 days; 2.60 in Q1FY27). Occupancy fell because new hospitals start nearly empty and because FY25-26 had weak infection seasons.

blocks.callout: **What would move the numbers:** each 1pp of occupancy on ~1,900 operational beds is ~6,900 bed-days, or ~₹45 cr of revenue at FY27E ARPOB. Management's 56-58% occupancy target on today's beds would add ~₹500 cr a year of revenue to our FY27E (~46% on the existing hospitals), without new capex. That is the upside case for the existing network; our forecasts reach ~50% on the existing hospitals by FY29E.

sections.title: Mature hospitals earn more per bed and fill better; new ones take years to catch up

blocks.p: Rainbow splits its network into **mature** hospitals (operating for 5+ years; from FY27 this includes Visakhapatnam and Hebbal: 1,550 capacity and 1,202 operational beds) and **new** hospitals (10 units under five years old, incl. the acquired Warangal and Guwahati: 885 capacity, 660 operational). In Q1FY27 mature hospitals ran at 45.0% occupancy and ₹70,662 ARPOB, new ones at 34.4% and ₹59,133. The company does not disclose EBITDA by cohort; it says greenfield hospitals take 12-18 months to break even (Rajahmundry is at breakeven, Electronic City close, HRBR loss-making), acquired ones were profitable from the start (Guwahati near the group margin), and the margin pressure from ~40% more beds in two years is "temporary".

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the cohort data show the model works: new hospitals do climb (occupancy +3.3pp in a year) and mature hospitals reprice (+10% ARPOB in Q1FY27, price plus mix). But it is slow: the new cohort averaged only 37.8% occupancy in FY26 (36.8% in FY25). With 1,200 more beds coming, the new cohort will stay a third or more of the network until FY30, which caps group occupancy and margins.

sections.title: The next 1,200 beds: Mumbai, Gurugram, Pune, Indore and more of the South

blocks.p: On 31-Jul-2026 management set out its biggest plan yet: ~2,500 more beds over five years (to ~5,000) for ~₹2,200 cr, all from internal cash, with ~1,200 beds already "visible". About 70% of the new beds go to markets where Rainbow is new or small (Delhi NCR, North and Central India, Mumbai); 30% to the South. Five hubs anchor the network: Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Gurugram and Guwahati. Three deals were announced the day before the Q1 call: a 100-bed brownfield hospital in Malad, Mumbai (a JV with three doctor-promoters), the 70-bed Prime Children's Hospital in Nellore (plus a 30-bed maternal block) and a 50-bed leased hospital in Guntur. Coimbatore has already slipped from end-FY27 to H2FY28.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Rainbow has a genuine moat in Hyderabad and Bengaluru: no other operator has built dedicated paediatric super-specialty networks of this depth, and the full-time doctor model and NICU/PICU capability are slow to copy. The moat is **local, not national**: it took Rainbow years to reach decent occupancy in Chennai ("some dip three years ago", CMD) and its Delhi presence after nine years is 24 beds of its own. The new markets have to be won from scratch against large multi-specialty chains with paediatric departments. And the moat protects **quality and price**, not **occupancy**: with births falling, filling beds depends on taking share.

sections.title: Revenue up 2.4x since FY20 and margins above 30%, but growth slowed to 12% in FY26

blocks.p: Rainbow's revenue grew from ₹719 cr in FY20 to ₹1,703 cr in FY26 (15% a year). FY21 fell 10% in the Covid lockdowns; FY22 jumped 50%, helped by ₹96 cr of one-off Covid-vaccine revenue. Since then growth has been 21%, 10%, 17% and 12%: slower in years when new hospitals were still filling (FY24) and when the paediatric infection season was weak (FY26). Profit attributable to shareholders rose from ₹138 cr (FY22) to ₹278 cr (FY26), ~19% a year, helped by rising interest income in FY23-25.

sections.title: A seasonal business: children fall sick in the monsoon and winter

blocks.p: Paediatric admissions rise with respiratory and vector-borne infections in the monsoon (July-September) and winter (October-December). So Q2 and Q3 are Rainbow's strong quarters and Q1 (April-June, summer holidays) the weakest: in FY25 occupancy was 42% in Q1 and 60% in Q2. Seasonal patients are mostly low-acuity and stay longer, so ARPOB moves the other way (lowest in Q2). FY26 had a weak season: Q2 occupancy fell to 52% from 60% and revenue grew only 7% in Q2 and 12% in Q3. Management says growth would have been 18-20% instead of 12% with a normal season, and that it is working to depend less on it.

sections.title: Self-funded growth so far; the next capex cycle is twice as large

blocks.p: Rainbow has funded its growth without debt. Over FY25-26 it generated ₹816 cr of operating cash, paid ₹183 cr of rent (lease payments), spent ₹362 cr on capex and ₹203 cr on two acquisitions, and paid ₹60 cr of dividends. Returns are good but falling: ROCE (Screener, post-Ind AS) was 23-24% in FY22-23 and 17% in FY26, as ~780 beds were added in two years. The company's own return on capital employed excluding cash was 23.7% in FY26 (26.0% in FY25). The next phase is bigger: ~₹2,200 cr over five years for ~2,500 beds (₹440 cr a year, twice FY26 capex).

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean, but read the Ind AS 116 and minority lines carefully

bullets: **Two EBITDA numbers.** Under Ind AS 116 rent is not an expense: FY26 EBITDA was ₹544 cr (32.0%) post-Ind AS but ₹449 cr (26.3%) after ₹96 cr of lease payments. Rent shows up as right-of-use depreciation (₹54 cr) and lease interest (₹78 cr, all of Rainbow's finance cost). Compare margins with other hospitals on the same basis; the street's targets use pre-Ind AS EBITDA (PL) or do not say.

**Doctor costs sit outside employee cost.** Full-time doctors are paid "professional fees" (₹419 cr, 24.6% of FY26 revenue; 26.3% in Q1FY27), on top of ₹234 cr of employee cost. The two together are ~38% of revenue.

**Minorities.** Since FY26 profit has a minority share (24% of Warangal and Guwahati: ₹3 cr in FY26, ₹2 cr in Q1FY27), and the Malad JV with doctors will add more. We use profit attributable to shareholders throughout.

**One-offs.** FY26 tax included a ₹13 cr deferred-tax credit at Rosewalk (Q4FY26; reported PAT +38%, ~+17% without it); a ₹1.5 cr Labour Code charge; FY22 revenue included ₹96 cr of Covid-vaccine sales.

**Cash conversion.** Operating cash flow was 77% of post-Ind AS EBITDA in FY26 (80% in FY25), but rent (₹96 cr) is paid out of financing cash flow; after rent, management puts conversion at ~72% of pre-Ind AS EBITDA.

**Other income** was ₹44 cr in FY26 (12% of pre-tax profit), mostly mutual-fund gains and deposit interest: it fell 14% as cash went into acquisitions, and we build it rather than extrapolate it (see Forecasts).
**Audit.** S.R. Batliboi & Associates (EY), unqualified; key audit matters were the accounting for the two acquisitions and a loan impairment test (standalone).

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: GREEN.** Simple, cash-generative and well disclosed (KPIs every quarter, pre- and post-Ind AS EBITDA). The traps are presentational: post-Ind AS margins flatter comparisons with pre-Ind AS peers, and doctor fees must be added to staff costs. Related-party dealings are small (~₹10 cr a year; see Governance).

sections.title: No borrowings, but ₹891 cr of lease liabilities: net cash on one basis, net debt on the other

blocks.p: Rainbow has no bank debt. It leases most of its hospital buildings (lease terms of 3-20 years; most new spokes are leased, the Gurugram projects are on owned land). Under Ind AS 116 the present value of future rent sits on the balance sheet as a lease liability: ₹891 cr at Mar-2026 (₹764 cr a year earlier; ₹146 cr of new leases in FY26), and rent appears as depreciation (₹54 cr) and interest (₹78 cr) rather than as an expense. Against this the company holds ₹594 cr of cash, bank deposits and debt mutual funds (₹613 cr at Jun-2026). So Rainbow has **net cash of ~₹600 cr ignoring leases**, or **net debt of ~₹300 cr including them**. Both are fine; what matters is using one basis consistently (see Valuation).

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Rainbow Children's Medicare (consolidated, ₹ crore). One reportable segment, so the engine runs on a single revenue-growth path and a post-Ind AS 116 EBITDA margin (Screener basis: rent is not in EBITDA; lease interest sits in interest and right-of-use depreciation in depreciation; lease liabilities sit in borrowings, so the model's net cash is net of leases). The bed build (mature hospitals, new hospitals, pipeline) sits in `businessLines`; the authoring script checks that it sums to model revenue. Profit is attributable to owners (RAINBOW.patch.js); the tax line carries the 24% minorities in the acquired hospitals. Valued on EV/EBITDA, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: From the bed build below (beds × 365 × occupancy × ARPOB, plus pipeline hospitals). FY27 +22%: Q1 +33% (organic ~24%; acquisitions ₹38 cr), Q2 guided 'above 20%', the acquisition boost fades from Q3 (Guwahati and Warangal were consolidated from Aug-25 and Jul-25) and the 2026 monsoon was late and deficient; management guides ~20% and 'cross ₹2,000 cr'. FY28 +21%, FY29 +20%: ARPOB +5-6% a year (management: ARPP 5-6%), occupancy of new hospitals rising from 34% toward the mid-40s, and the pipeline (Malad, Coimbatore, Gurugram, Pune) starting with low occupancy. Management's medium-term ambition is ~20% a year (double revenue in four years after FY27).

businessLines._why: Mature = the 1,202 operational beds that management classifies as mature from FY27 (Q1FY27: occupancy 45.0%, ARPOB ₹70,662). Full-year occupancy has run ~6-8pp above Q1 (FY25 50.5% vs 42.4%; FY26 46.3% vs 40.2%) and ARPOB ~2-5% below Q1, so FY27 mature = 50.5% and ₹67,500 (a normal-to-weak season after a late monsoon), then +1-1.5pp of occupancy and +5-6% ARPOB a year (still below the 56% mature occupancy of FY25). New = the 10 hospitals under five years old (Q1FY27: 660 operational of 885 capacity beds, occupancy 34.4%, ARPOB ₹59,133): operational beds rise as HRBR, Electronic City and Warangal fill (690 / 760 / 800 weighted), occupancy 38% / 43% / 46%, ARPOB ₹57,000 / 60,400 / 63,500. Pipeline revenue is GAM's estimate per hospital (beds × months open × ~25-45% occupancy × ₹45,000-85,000 ARPOB, by city), using the opening dates management gave on 31-Jul-2026; we assume slow ramps for the Gurugram hub and Pune.

assumptions._marginWhy: Post-Ind AS EBITDA margin (Screener basis): 33% FY24-25, 32.2% FY26, 28.7% in Q1FY27 (29.5% a year earlier). Management guides the pre-Ind AS margin back to 24-25% for FY27 (Q1FY27 23.0%; FY26 26.3%); rent is ~5pp of revenue (Ind AS impact ₹96 cr in FY26, ₹26 cr in Q1FY27), so 24.5-25% pre-Ind AS ≈ 29.7-30.2% post. FY28 30.5%: HRBR and Electronic City break even (12-18 months guided), offset by start-up losses at Malad, Coimbatore and Gurugram Sector 56. FY29 30.0%: the 325-bed Gurugram hub, Pune and Seegehalli open. Each 1pp of margin is ~₹25 cr of FY28E EBITDA (~5% of EPS).
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex ₹380 / 460 / 480 cr plus new leases (right-of-use additions) ₹100 / 120 / 100 cr. Cash: maintenance ~₹45 cr a year; Gurugram ₹400-500 cr over two years (own land, own build); other projects at ₹65-70 lakh a bed (Coimbatore 130, Pune 150, Indore 100, Seegehalli 80, Malad fit-out); five-year plan ₹2,200 cr for 2,500 beds (~₹440 cr a year). FY26 capex ₹217 cr, Q1FY27 ₹56 cr. New leases are added because the model's net debt includes lease liabilities: right-of-use additions were ₹146 cr in FY26 (AR note 2.32), and Guntur, Malad, Indore and Seegehalli are leased. Engine workaround: a new lease adds an asset and a liability without cash, which the engine can only show as capex funded from net cash. The Nellore acquisition price is not disclosed and is left out.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹151 cr (incl. right-of-use depreciation ₹54 cr) = 6.6% of average gross block (₹2,294 cr); Q1FY27 ₹42 cr (₹169 cr annualised). 6.5% gives FY27E ≈ ₹181 cr with the new hospitals; the engine depreciates capex at once while projects sit in CWIP.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Set to zero because the engine applies the yield to net cash after lease liabilities, which is negative (₹583 cr of cash, deposits and investments less ₹891 cr of leases at Mar-26). Treasury income is built on gross cash in `otherIncome` instead.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (AR FY26 note 2.21). (1) Treasury income = yield × opening gross cash, deposits and mutual funds: FY26 ₹38.4 cr (bank interest ₹8.0 cr + mutual-fund gains ₹30.4 cr) on ~₹645 cr average funds = ~6.0%; company cash & investments ₹594 cr (Mar-26) and ₹613 cr (Jun-26). We take 6.25% on ₹594 / 600 / 610 cr opening funds (capex roughly absorbs free cash flow): ₹37 / 37.5 / 38 cr. (2) Recurring non-treasury interest (loans ₹1.7 cr and other financial assets ₹1.9 cr, unchanged FY25-26): ₹3.6 cr, held at ₹4-5 cr. One-offs left out: asset-sale gain ₹1.2 cr, write-backs ₹0.5 cr, FX. FY27E ₹41 cr vs FY26 ₹43.8 cr and the twelve months to Jun-26 ₹36.5 cr (Screener).

otherTreasury._why: Bank deposits reported under other financial assets, not in Screener's cash or investments: ₹104 cr non-current + ₹49 cr current at Mar-26 (AR notes 2.3a/b) less ₹7.8 cr earmarked for CSR and bank guarantees. With Screener's cash (₹34 cr) and mutual funds (₹404 cr) this gives the company's ₹583-594 cr.

assumptions._interestWhy: All finance cost is lease interest: ₹77.6 cr in FY26 on ₹764-891 cr of lease liabilities (~9%); ₹21.2 cr in Q1FY27 (₹85 cr annualised). New leases (~₹100-120 cr a year) add ~₹9-10 cr a year.
assumptions._taxWhy: Tax plus minorities (engine workaround: there is no minority line). Q1FY27: PBT ₹84.0 cr, tax ₹21.4 cr (25.5%), attributable PAT ₹60.6 cr = 27.8% leakage (minorities ~2.3%). FY26 effective tax 21.4% included a one-off ₹13 cr deferred-tax credit at Rosewalk; underlying ~25.5%. Minorities: 24% of Prashanthi and Pratiksha (₹3 cr in FY26, ₹2 cr in Q1FY27); the Malad JV with doctors adds more from FY28.
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividend ~13-14% of profit since listing (₹3 a share paid in FY26, ₹30 cr); capex absorbs the rest.

dcf._betaWhy: No borrowings; lease liabilities are ~6% of enterprise value, so WACC (~11.0-11.1%) is close to the 11.3% cost of equity the engine uses. Defensive demand, but expansion risk outside the home markets.
dcf._tgWhy: Births are flat in India, but paediatric and maternity care is moving to organised, specialised hospitals and prices rise 5-6% a year: 6% nominal, the top of the house range.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades from ~20% to 9% by year 15: bed additions slow and the network matures.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 31% post-Ind AS (~26% pre-Ind AS): back near FY26 once the 2026-29 openings mature, but below FY24-25 (33%) as more beds sit in costlier markets (NCR, Mumbai).
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex incl. new leases falls from ~19-23% of revenue (expansion) to 11%: replacement of the asset base (depreciation ~8.5% of revenue) plus growth capex for 6-9% growth.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: A normal paediatric season returns, new hospitals reach 45%+ occupancy a year early, Mumbai and Gurugram open on time with high-acuity mix, and the margin recovers toward 32% (pre-Ind AS ~26.5%).

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Two more weak seasons, occupancy stuck near 41-45%, the expansion outside the South (NCR, Mumbai, Pune, Indore) ramps slowly and burns cash, and the margin falls toward 28% (pre-Ind AS ~23%).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: How the street values Rainbow: EV/EBITDA on FY28E (Prabhudas Lilladher 28x pre-Ind AS EBITDA, ICICI Securities 25x, Anand Rathi 22x). We use post-Ind AS EBITDA with lease liabilities in net debt (the model basis; consistent because rent is excluded from EBITDA and the lease debt is counted). 20x = Rainbow's 21.5x median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since listing (May-2022; no trough years: forward EBITDA never fell below half its prior peak), cut by the 7.4% median de-rating of six listed hospital peers versus their five-year median EV/EBITDA on 30-Sep-2026 (Apollo, Max, Fortis, Narayana, Medanta, Jupiter; KIMS and Aster left out because new-hospital losses and the 2024 GCC demerger distort their history) = 19.9x, rounded to 20x. No growth adjustment: our faster EBITDA growth (~18% a year FY26-29E vs 11% FY23-26) is bought with capex into new markets at lower returns. Bull 24.5x and bear 18x = the 75th and 25th percentiles of its forward EV/EBITDA since listing.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check on earnings. 39x = Rainbow's 44.9x median one-year-forward P/E since listing (forwardMedian; no trough years) cut by the 13.5% median P/E de-rating of the same six hospital peers versus their five-year medians on 30-Sep-2026 (38.8x). Bull 47x, bear 32x scale with the EV/EBITDA multiples.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF (capex includes new leases), Ke 11.3%, terminal growth 6%, less net lease liabilities.
